options: A single asset's physical storage room
A grouping of assets that share the same accounting treatment
The name of an asset book
A type of journal entry created during retirement
questions.explain: A category groups assets with the same depreciation method, life, and GL accounts so those rules don't need to be re-entered for every asset.

options: A printed manual listing every asset category
The combination of a category and a specific asset book, which carries the actual default rules
A report showing all categories in the company
A synonym for a budget book
questions.explain: Categories are configured per book. The category book — category plus book — is where default depreciation rules actually live, not the category alone.

questions.q: Why might the same category have different depreciation rules in a corporate book versus a tax book?
options: It can't — categories must be identical across all books
Because corporate and tax reporting legitimately require different depreciation treatment for the same assets
Because tax books don't support categories
Because categories are deleted when copied to a tax book
questions.explain: A corporate book and a tax book can depreciate the same category of asset differently, such as straight-line versus an accelerated method, to meet each reporting requirement.

questions.q: Which of these is typically defaulted by a category book onto a new asset?
options: The employee who will use the asset
The invoice number from Payables
The depreciation method and useful life
The asset's serial number
questions.explain: Category books default the depreciation method, useful life, prorate convention, and GL accounts onto new assets in that category.

questions.q: What is the risk of designing categories that are too granular (e.g., one per model number)?
options: Depreciation can no longer be calculated at all
It creates a maintenance burden with no real accounting benefit
It automatically triggers impairment
It prevents assets from ever being retired
questions.explain: Overly granular categories multiply setup and maintenance work without providing any additional accounting precision that matters.
